trickyParts: The session reader's output handling is where a transcript is easiest to corrupt: psql's aligned and quoted formats would mangle JSONL, so it runs -A -t; the capture is $(psql … && printf x) so the session's own trailing newlines survive the substitution, with psql's one closing newline then taken off; and an empty answer is what distinguishes a session the table does not hold from a short one, which is what lets the reader fail naming the path as the old cat did.

One generation counter for every name, not one per name: a per-name counter deleted with its record would read the same before a strand as after its unstrand, which is exactly the window it exists to catch. A bump for another issue costs one Uncertain and a re-evaluation a tick later.

discoveredComplexity: The deleted-world sweep's honest result is that two of its four categories were already clean, and clean for a reason: the recovery vocabulary survives only as negative assertions — the lost-volume line must never appear, the recovery marker must never exist — and Stage 4a reads a marker rather than transcripts, which is why the marker path was its only tie to the old world. A category checked and found clean, with its command, is reported as clean rather than padded to look like a wider fix.

A build Job in this namespace is admitted only with activeDeadlineSeconds and ttlSecondsAfterFinished on both the Job and its pod template, automountServiceAccountToken false, runtimeClassName gvisor, the build compute class, and at least 4 CPU; ConfigMaps are forbidden, so a script reaches the pod base64-encoded in its command. That is what it took to exercise the reader's SQL against a real Postgres from a worker pod, and it is worth knowing for the next role that needs a database.
